metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (Java) with a deployable entry point (@WebService JAX-WS endpoint deployed on JBoss AS 5.1) and an API contract (WSDL). Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: The service writes to a persistent data store (Oracle 11g via JDBC INSERT into partner_orders) through a synchronous SOAP endpoint. It owns its data and exposes a write operation. Classified as stateful-crud.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 1.22 yields Not Ready band but 11 High findings (below the 12 threshold) yield Remediation Required tier. Five surface-gated questions (INF-Q9, SEC-Q1, OPS-Q5, OPS-Q7, OPS-Q9) were excluded from evaluation because has_deployed_workload=false and has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false. If evaluated, these would likely increase High count to ≥12, aligning both metrics to Not Ready.

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: All compute runs on JBoss AS 5.1 deployed on RHEL 6 (both EOL). No managed container orchestration (ECS/EKS), no serverless (Lambda), no Fargate.
findings.gap: Zero managed compute adoption. The entire runtime stack is end-of-life with no path to managed services.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the service targeting ECS/Fargate or Lambda. Given the single-endpoint nature, Lambda behind API Gateway is the most cost-effective option.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: Database is self-managed Oracle 11g accessed via hardcoded JDBC connection string. No managed database services (RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB) in use. Oracle 11g is past EOL.
findings.gap: Entirely self-managed database with no automated failover, no managed patching, no automated backups visible.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL. The SQL used is standard INSERT — no proprietary Oracle SQL detected, making migration straightforward.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: No workflow orchestration service in use. The entire business operation is implemented as sequential inline code in a single method with a try/catch block.
findings.gap: All logic is hardcoded in application code with no orchestration, no retry logic, no error recovery beyond returning raw exception text.
findings.recommendation: When rewriting, implement order processing as a Step Functions workflow if additional steps are needed (validation, partner notification, fulfillment).

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure exists. The service performs a synchronous SOAP request to DB INSERT to synchronous response with no event emission on state changes.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries. Order creation events are not published.
findings.recommendation: Introduce SQS or EventBridge for order creation events. Publish events that downstream consumers can process asynchronously.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No network security configuration exists. The WSDL specifies a plain HTTP endpoint with no TLS. No VPC definitions, no security groups, no network ACLs.
findings.gap: No VPC, no private subnets, no security groups, no TLS. Service exposed over plain HTTP.
findings.recommendation: Deploy in a VPC with private subnets. Use an ALB or API Gateway with TLS termination. Configure least-privilege security groups.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: The SOAP service is exposed directly on JBoss port 8080 with no API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront in front.
findings.gap: No managed entry point — direct service exposure with no throttling, no rate limiting, no centralized auth.
findings.recommendation: Place an API Gateway or ALB in front of the service with request validation, throttling, and WAF integration.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling configuration exists. The service runs on a single JBoss instance with static capacity.
findings.gap: All capacity is statically provisioned. Cannot respond to traffic spikes or scale down during low demand.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to managed compute (ECS/Lambda), configure auto-scaling with appropriate thresholds.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration exists in the repository. The Oracle 11g database has no visible backup automation.
findings.gap: No automated backups, no defined retention periods, no tested restore procedures.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to RDS/Aurora, enable automated backups with 7+ day retention and point-in-time recovery.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: Zero IaC coverage. No Terraform files, no CloudFormation templates, no CDK stacks. All infrastructure is manually provisioned.
findings.gap: No IaC — 0% coverage. All infrastructure created manually. No reproducibility, no environment consistency.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in CDK or Terraform: compute, database, networking, and operational resources.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. The README confirms the build process is manual: Ant with wsgen/wsimport run by hand. No build file is even present.
findings.gap: No CI/CD automation — all builds and deployments are manual. No automated testing, no quality gates.
findings.recommendation: Implement a CI/CD pipeline (CodePipeline + CodeBuild) with build, test, security scan, and deploy stages.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Java 6 (EOL since 2013) with JAX-WS framework (legacy SOAP). No AWS SDK. Compound legacy signals across language version, framework, and SDK axes.
findings.gap: Java 6 is 3 major LTS versions behind current. JAX-WS RPC/encoded is deprecated. No modern framework or AWS SDK.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Java 17+ with Spring Boot 3.x and AWS SDK v2.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: The application is a single class with a single method performing all operations inline: XML parsing, field extraction, JDBC connection, SQL execution, and error handling. Zero separation of concerns.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with no clear module boundaries. Business logic, data access, and protocol handling interleaved in a single method.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite with clean architecture: separate protocol adapter, domain logic, and data access layer. Use Hexagonal Architecture.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: All communication is synchronous SOAP. No async patterns, no message queues, no event publishing. For a stateful-crud service creating order records, no ability to decouple order acceptance from processing.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous with no async patterns. No event-driven integration possible.
findings.recommendation: Implement async order processing: accept synchronously, process via SQS, emit events to EventBridge.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: All operations are synchronous regardless of duration. No async job processing, no status polling, no callback mechanism. The caller must hold the SOAP connection open for the entire operation.
findings.gap: No async job processing. All operations synchronous regardless of duration.
findings.recommendation: Implement async submission pattern: accept order (return tracking ID), process asynchronously, provide status endpoint.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API versioning. The WSDL defines a single namespace with no version indicator. The endpoint URL has no version segment.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes deployed directly to all partners.
findings.recommendation: Implement API versioning in the modernized service (URL path versioning: /v1/orders).

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: All service endpoints are hardcoded. The WSDL has a hardcoded service address. The database connection string is hardcoded in source code. No service registry or dynamic discovery.
findings.gap: All endpoints hardcoded in source and WSDL. Relocating the service or database requires code changes.
findings.recommendation: Externalize endpoints to environment variables or Parameter Store. Use Route 53 or Cloud Map for service discovery.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: Partner order XML is received as a raw string, parsed in-memory, and discarded after field extraction. No S3 or managed object storage. Original documents are lost after processing.
findings.gap: No document archival. Original purchase order XML not stored in managed object storage.
findings.recommendation: Archive original purchase order XML to S3 before processing. Enable versioning and lifecycle policies.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: No data access layer exists. Database access via raw JDBC directly in the endpoint method with string-concatenated SQL. No ORM, no DAO pattern, no repository abstraction.
findings.gap: Database queries directly in the endpoint handler with no abstraction. SQL built via string concatenation.
findings.recommendation: Implement a repository/DAO pattern with parameterized queries. Use Spring Data JPA or jOOQ.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: Oracle 11g detected from JDBC connection string and README. Oracle 11g reached end of extended support in 2021. No IaC version pinning.
findings.gap: Database engine past EOL. No version pinning. Running on unsupported engine with known vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Aurora PostgreSQL (current, fully managed). Use AWS SCT for schema analysis and DMS for migration.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest configured. Oracle 11g accessed via plain JDBC with no evidence of TDE or encryption. Partner order data stored unencrypted.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest — partner data stored in plaintext.
findings.recommendation: Enable encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS key when migrating to RDS/Aurora.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: Authentication uses WS-Security username token with password in plaintext over HTTP. Static credential authentication, not token-based.
findings.gap: Static credential auth (WS-Security PasswordText) without token-based auth. Credentials in plaintext over HTTP.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT-based authentication. Use API Gateway authorizers with Cognito. Enforce TLS.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: Application manages authentication independently. Partner credentials stored in a flat properties file. No IdP integration, no SSO, no federation.
findings.gap: No centralized identity integration. Partner credentials in flat file.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito or centralized IdP for partner authentication.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: Plaintext database credentials hardcoded directly in source code: DB_USER = "partner_app" and DB_PASS = "partner2009". Committed to version control.
findings.gap: Hardcoded plaintext credentials in source code — most critical secrets management failure.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate credentials. Store all secrets in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching strategy or vulnerability scanning. Runtime stack entirely EOL: RHEL 6, JBoss AS 5.1, Java 6. No SSM, no Inspector, no Dependabot.
findings.gap: No patching automation, no vulnerability scanning, EOL OS and application server.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to managed compute (ECS/Lambda) for automatic OS patching. Enable ECR scanning and Dependabot.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools. No CI/CD pipeline exists. Known vulnerabilities (XXE, SQL injection) present and undetected by automated tooling.
findings.gap: No SAST, no dependency scanning, no container scanning. Known vulnerabilities undetected.
findings.recommendation: Implement SAST (SonarQube/Semgrep) and dependency scanning in CI/CD. Block deployments on critical findings.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing instrumented. No OpenTelemetry SDK, no X-Ray, no trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No ability to trace requests through the service or correlate with downstream systems.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with OpenTelemetry SDK or AWS X-Ray. Propagate trace IDs across service boundaries.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency targets, no error rate thresholds, no monitoring artifacts.
findings.gap: No formal SLO definitions, no error budgets, no monitoring.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for order submission (p99 latency, availability, error rate). Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business event tracking. Cannot measure business impact or order processing health.
findings.gap: No business metrics — only default JBoss/OS metrics if any monitoring configured externally.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom CloudWatch metrics: orders per partner, acceptance rate, processing latency, error rate.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration.
findings.gap: No alerting — no static thresholds, no anomaly detection.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms on error rates and latency. Enable anomaly detection. Integrate with alerting tool.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. README states: 'No tests; partner onboarding is a manual SOAP-UI session.' Zero test coverage.
findings.gap: No automated tests — no integration tests, no unit tests, no contract tests.
findings.recommendation: Write integration tests for order submission workflow. Use contract testing for the API interface. Include in CI pipeline.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards, no alarms with named owners, no CODEOWNERS file, no monitoring infrastructure.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — monitoring entirely absent.
findings.recommendation: Define service-level dashboards and alarms with named owners. Create CODEOWNERS file.

decomposition_strategy.rationale: Single endpoint, entire technology stack EOL, zero tests, critical security vulnerabilities, no build system. Service is small enough (~50 lines of logic) that rewriting is lower-risk than modernizing in place.
decomposition_strategy.effort_estimate: 4-8 weeks for complete rewrite with proper architecture, tests, CI/CD, and IaC
